what: Takeda is Japan's largest pharmaceutical company. It focuses on gastrointestinal and inflammatory disease, rare diseases, neuroscience, oncology and plasma-derived therapies, and became global after buying Shire.
customers: Health systems, hospitals, insurers and governments in Japan, the United States and Europe.
money: Entyvio for inflammatory bowel disease and related medicines
hereditary angioedema, enzyme replacement and ADHD medicines
moat: Plasma collection and manufacturing, which takes years to build and is hard to copy, plus rare-disease medicines with few alternatives.
risks: It reported a small net loss margin last year after impairment and amortisation charges
Revenue fell about 8% as older medicines lost exclusivity
Debt of about $29 billion against under $3 billion of cash, left from the Shire purchase
Vyvanse for ADHD now faces generic competition in the US
opportunities: A late-stage pipeline in inflammatory bowel disease, narcolepsy and celiac disease
Plasma therapy demand grows steadily and supply is constrained industry-wide
Cost programmes are intended to restore margins as the pipeline arrives
watch: Late-stage trial results and whether revenue returns to growth as new medicines launch.
